```{python}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Imports & configuration"

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from plotly.subplots import make_subplots
import warnings
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")

# ── File paths ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DATA_DIR = "data/raw"
PATH_PBP      = DATA_DIR + "/pbp_game_stats.csv"
PATH_WTS      = DATA_DIR + "/weekly_team_stats.csv"
PATH_SCH      = DATA_DIR + "/schedules.csv"
PATH_ADV_PASS = DATA_DIR + "/adv_passing.csv"
PATH_ADV_RUSH = DATA_DIR + "/adv_rushing.csv"
PATH_ADV_DEF  = DATA_DIR + "/adv_defense.csv"

OTC_DIR = "data/over_the_cap"
PATH_OTC_SPENDING  = OTC_DIR + "/otc_positional_spending.csv"
PATH_OTC_CONTRACTS = OTC_DIR + "/otc_player_contracts.csv"
# Note: OTC data is used only in the post-model supplementary analysis (Part VII).
# It is not used in any model training, feature engineering, or prediction.

# ── Colour palette ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
BLUE   = "#2563EB"
RED    = "#DC2626"
TEAL   = "#0D9488"
AMBER  = "#D97706"
SLATE  = "#94A3B8"
BORDER = "#E2E8F0"
BEARS  = "#0B162A"
GREEN  = "#16A34A"
PURPLE = "#7C3AED"

def clean_fig(fig, height=420, margin=None):
    if margin is None:
        margin = dict(l=48, r=24, t=32, b=48)
    fig.update_layout(
        height=height, margin=margin,
        paper_bgcolor="white", plot_bgcolor="white",
        font=dict(family="Inter, system-ui, sans-serif", size=13, color="#1E293B"),
        showlegend=False,
    )
    fig.update_xaxes(showgrid=False, zeroline=False, linecolor=BORDER,
                     tickcolor=BORDER, tickfont_color=SLATE)
    fig.update_yaxes(showgrid=True, gridcolor=BORDER, zeroline=False,
                     linecolor=BORDER, tickfont_color=SLATE)
    return fig
```

# Part I — Exploratory Data Analysis

## 1. Data loading & cleaning

All data comes from Pro Football Reference via nflverse. The analysis covers
**2018–2025 regular seasons** — 2018 is the earliest year PFR publishes advanced
tracking stats (pressure rates, yards after contact, coverage metrics), so using
data prior to that would mean running the model on an incomplete feature set.


```{python}
#| label: data-load
#| code-summary: "Load and clean raw files"

pbp      = pd.read_csv(PATH_PBP)
wts      = pd.read_csv(PATH_WTS)
sch      = pd.read_csv(PATH_SCH)
adv_pass = pd.read_csv(PATH_ADV_PASS)
adv_rush = pd.read_csv(PATH_ADV_RUSH)
adv_def  = pd.read_csv(PATH_ADV_DEF)

# ── Clean weekly_team_stats
wts = wts[wts["recent_team"] != wts["opponent_team"]].copy()
wts["season_type"] = wts["season_type"].str[:3]
wts = wts[wts["season_type"] == "REG"].copy()
wts = wts.rename(columns={"recent_team": "team", "opponent_team": "opponent"})

print(f"pbp:      {len(pbp):>6,} rows | seasons {pbp['season'].min()}–{pbp['season'].max()}")
print(f"wts:      {len(wts):>6,} rows | seasons {wts['season'].min()}–{wts['season'].max()}")
print(f"sch:      {len(sch):>6,} rows | seasons {sch['season'].min()}–{sch['season'].max()}")
print(f"adv_pass: {len(adv_pass):>6,} rows | seasons {adv_pass['season'].min()}–{adv_pass['season'].max()}")
print(f"adv_rush: {len(adv_rush):>6,} rows | seasons {adv_rush['season'].min()}–{adv_rush['season'].max()}")
print(f"adv_def:  {len(adv_def):>6,} rows | seasons {adv_def['season'].min()}–{adv_def['season'].max()}")
```

```{python}
#| label: build-long
#| code-summary: "Build 2-rows-per-game master table"

def build_long_games(sch):
    """
    Reshape schedule from 1 row per game to 2 rows per game.
    total_line is carried through alongside spread_line_team
    so it is available as a vegas feature later.
    """
    DIVISIONS = {
        "AFC East":  {"BUF","MIA","NE","NYJ"},
        "AFC North": {"BAL","CIN","CLE","PIT"},
        "AFC South": {"HOU","IND","JAX","TEN"},
        "AFC West":  {"DEN","KC","LV","LAC"},
        "NFC East":  {"DAL","NYG","PHI","WAS"},
        "NFC North": {"CHI","DET","GB","MIN"},
        "NFC South": {"ATL","CAR","NO","TB"},
        "NFC West":  {"ARI","LAR","SEA","SF"},
    }
    team_div = {}
    for div, teams in DIVISIONS.items():
        for t in teams:
            team_div[t] = div

    home = sch.copy().rename(columns={
        "home_team":"team", "away_team":"opponent",
        "home_score":"team_score", "away_score":"opp_score",
        "home_rest":"rest", "away_rest":"opp_rest"})
    home["is_home"] = 1
    home["spread_line_team"] = home["spread_line"]

    away = sch.copy().rename(columns={
        "away_team":"team", "home_team":"opponent",
        "away_score":"team_score", "home_score":"opp_score",
        "away_rest":"rest", "home_rest":"opp_rest"})
    away["is_home"] = 0
    away["spread_line_team"] = -away["spread_line"]

    g = pd.concat([home, away], ignore_index=True)
    g["win"] = np.where(
        g["team_score"].notna(),
        (g["team_score"] > g["opp_score"]).astype(float),
        np.nan)
    g["point_diff"] = g["team_score"] - g["opp_score"]
    g["favoured"]   = (g["spread_line_team"] > 0).astype(int)

    # net rest differential
    g["net_rest_diff"] = g["rest"] - g["opp_rest"]

    # capped point margin
    g["point_diff_capped"] = g["point_diff"].clip(-21, 21)

    # division game flag
    g["is_division_game"] = (
        g.apply(lambda r: int(team_div.get(r["team"],"") ==
                               team_div.get(r["opponent"],"") and
                               team_div.get(r["team"],"") != ""), axis=1)
    )

    return g

games = build_long_games(sch)
games = games[games["season"] >= 2018].copy()

home_key = sch[["game_id","season","week","home_team","away_team"]].rename(
    columns={"home_team":"team","away_team":"opponent"})
away_key = sch[["game_id","season","week","home_team","away_team"]].rename(
    columns={"away_team":"team","home_team":"opponent"})
wts = wts.merge(pd.concat([home_key, away_key]),
                on=["season","week","team","opponent"], how="inner")

print(f"Game rows (2018-2025): {len(games):,} | unique games: {games['game_id'].nunique():,}")
div_pct = games["is_division_game"].mean()
print(f"Division games: {div_pct:.1%} of rows ({games['is_division_game'].sum():,} team-rows)")
```

```{python}
#| label: assemble
#| code-summary: "Join all sources into unified game-level stats table"

def assemble_game_stats(games, wts, pbp, adv_pass, adv_rush, adv_def):
    g = games.sort_values(["season","week","game_id","team"]).copy()

    g = g.merge(pbp[["game_id","team","third_down_att","third_down_conv",
                      "turnovers_total","fumbles_lost","interceptions",
                      "time_of_possession_sec","first_downs_total",
                      "penalty_count","penalty_yards"]],
                on=["game_id","team"], how="left")

    opp_def = adv_def[["game_id","team","def_targets","def_completions_allowed",
                        "def_yards_allowed","def_receiving_td_allowed","def_ints"]].rename(
        columns={"team":"opponent", "def_targets":"pass_att_recon",
                 "def_completions_allowed":"completions_recon",
                 "def_yards_allowed":"passing_yards_recon",
                 "def_receiving_td_allowed":"passing_tds_recon",
                 "def_ints":"ints_thrown_recon"})
    g = g.merge(opp_def, on=["game_id","opponent"], how="left")

    rush = adv_rush[["game_id","team","carries","rushing_yards_before_contact",
                      "rushing_yards_after_contact","rushing_broken_tackles"]].copy()
    rush["rushing_yards_recon"] = (rush["rushing_yards_before_contact"]
                                   + rush["rushing_yards_after_contact"])
    g = g.merge(rush, on=["game_id","team"], how="left")

    g = g.merge(adv_pass[["game_id","team","passing_drops","passing_bad_throws",
                           "times_sacked","times_hurried","times_hit","times_pressured"]],
                on=["game_id","team"], how="left")

    g = g.merge(adv_def[["game_id","team","def_targets","def_completions_allowed",
                          "def_yards_allowed","def_receiving_td_allowed","def_ints",
                          "def_sacks","def_pressures","def_tackles_combined",
                          "def_missed_tackles","def_yards_after_catch"]],
                on=["game_id","team"], how="left", suffixes=("","_def"))

    g = g.merge(wts[["game_id","team","passing_yards","completions","attempts",
                      "sacks","sack_yards","rushing_yards"]],
                on=["game_id","team"], how="left")

    g["pass_yards"] = g["passing_yards"].fillna(g["passing_yards_recon"])
    g["pass_att"]   = g["attempts"].fillna(g["pass_att_recon"])
    g["pass_cmp"]   = g["completions"].fillna(g["completions_recon"])
    g["sack_count"] = g["sacks"].fillna(g["times_sacked"])
    g["sack_yds"]   = g["sack_yards"].fillna(g["times_sacked"] * 7)
    g["rush_yards"] = g["rushing_yards"].fillna(g["rushing_yards_recon"])

    dropbacks = (g["pass_att"] + g["sack_count"]).replace(0, np.nan)
    g["net_ypa"]         = (g["pass_yards"] - g["sack_yds"]) / dropbacks
    g["comp_pct"]        = g["pass_cmp"] / g["pass_att"].replace(0, np.nan)
    g["yds_per_carry"]   = g["rush_yards"] / g["carries"].replace(0, np.nan)
    # Net yards per play — used as the ELO update signal.
    # Formula: (net passing yards + rushing yards) / (dropbacks + carries)
    # Net passing yards = pass_yards - sack_yds  (same as net_ypa numerator)
    # This is deliberately net so sacks penalise the offense and reward the defense,
    # which is consistent with how net_ypa treats pass rush in the rolling features.
    total_plays = (dropbacks + g["carries"]).replace(0, np.nan)
    g["yds_per_play"] = (g["pass_yards"] - g["sack_yds"] + g["rush_yards"]) / total_plays
    g["third_down_rate"] = g["third_down_conv"] / g["third_down_att"].replace(0, np.nan)
    g["pressure_rate"]   = g["times_pressured"] / dropbacks
    g["bad_throw_rate"]  = g["passing_bad_throws"] / g["pass_att"].replace(0, np.nan)
    g["drop_rate"]       = g["passing_drops"] / g["pass_att"].replace(0, np.nan)
    g["yac_per_carry"]   = g["rushing_yards_after_contact"] / g["carries"].replace(0, np.nan)

    g["def_comp_pct"]      = g["def_completions_allowed"] / g["def_targets"].replace(0, np.nan)
    g["def_yds_per_tgt"]   = g["def_yards_allowed"] / g["def_targets"].replace(0, np.nan)
    g["def_pressure_rate"] = g["def_pressures"] / (g["def_targets"] + g["def_sacks"]).replace(0, np.nan)
    g["def_miss_tkl_pct"]  = g["def_missed_tackles"] / g["def_tackles_combined"].replace(0, np.nan)
    g["def_yac_allowed"]   = g["def_yards_after_catch"] / g["def_completions_allowed"].replace(0, np.nan)

    opp_to = (g[["game_id","team","turnovers_total"]].dropna()
               .rename(columns={"team":"opponent","turnovers_total":"opp_turnovers"}))
    g = g.merge(opp_to, on=["game_id","opponent"], how="left")
    g["turnover_margin"] = g["opp_turnovers"] - g["turnovers_total"]

    return g.reset_index(drop=True)

g = assemble_game_stats(games, wts, pbp, adv_pass, adv_rush, adv_def)
played = g[g["win"].notna() & g["season"].between(2018, 2025)].copy()

print(f"Full dataset:        {len(g):,} rows")
print(f"Played 2018-2025:    {len(played):,} rows")
print(f"2025 played:         {g[(g['season']==2025) & g['win'].notna()]['game_id'].nunique()} games")
```

## 1b. Playoff stakes flags

Week 18 games are structurally different: teams that have already clinched or
been eliminated have no incentive to win. We compute four binary flags from
the cumulative standings **before** each game is played.

```{python}
#| label: stakes
#| code-summary: "Compute playoff-stakes flags from cumulative standings"

def compute_stakes(g):
    """
    Compute pre-game playoff-clinch and elimination flags with NO leakage.

    Fix vs earlier versions
    -----------------------
    A prior implementation built cumulative standings across all games first,
    then assigned those final-season totals back to every game row — causing
    look-ahead leakage: a Week 3 game would see standings that included
    Weeks 4-18 results.

    Correct approach
    ----------------
    Process games in strict chronological order. Before processing game G,
    snapshot each team's current win/loss total (the true pre-game state).
    Then update running totals AFTER snapshotting. This guarantees that the
    flag for any game never includes that game's result or any future result.

    Clinch proxy    : cumulative wins   >= 10 before this game
    Elimination proxy: cumulative losses >= 10 before this game
    """
    running  = {}   # (season, team) -> {"wins": int, "losses": int}
    pre_game = {}   # (game_id, team) -> {"wins": int, "losses": int}

    # All unique games in strict chronological order
    played_games = (
        g[g["win"].notna()]
        .sort_values(["season", "week", "game_id"])
        .drop_duplicates("game_id", keep="first")[["game_id", "season", "week"]]
    )

    for _, gr in played_games.iterrows():
        gid    = gr["game_id"]
        season = gr["season"]
        game_rows = g[g["game_id"] == gid][["team", "win"]].dropna(subset=["win"])
        if len(game_rows) != 2:
            continue

        # Snapshot BEFORE updating — true pre-game state
        for _, tr in game_rows.iterrows():
            key = (season, tr["team"])
            running.setdefault(key, {"wins": 0, "losses": 0})
            pre_game[(gid, tr["team"])] = running[key].copy()

        # Update running totals AFTER snapshotting
        for _, tr in game_rows.iterrows():
            key = (season, tr["team"])
            if int(tr["win"]) == 1:
                running[key]["wins"]   += 1
            else:
                running[key]["losses"] += 1

    rows = []
    for _, row in g.iterrows():
        pre     = pre_game.get((row["game_id"], row["team"]),
                               {"wins": 0, "losses": 0})
        opp_pre = pre_game.get((row["game_id"], row["opponent"]),
                               {"wins": 0, "losses": 0})
        clinched   = int(pre["wins"]       >= 10)
        eliminated = int(pre["losses"]     >= 10)
        opp_clin   = int(opp_pre["wins"]   >= 10)
        opp_elim   = int(opp_pre["losses"] >= 10)
        rows.append({
            "game_id":         row["game_id"],
            "team":            row["team"],
            "team_clinched":   clinched,
            "team_eliminated": eliminated,
            "opp_clinched":    opp_clin,
            "opp_eliminated":  opp_elim,
            "game_low_stakes": int(clinched or eliminated or opp_clin or opp_elim),
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows)

stakes_df = compute_stakes(g)
g = g.merge(stakes_df, on=["game_id","team"], how="left")
for col in ["team_clinched","team_eliminated","opp_clinched","opp_eliminated","game_low_stakes"]:
    g[col] = g[col].fillna(0).astype(int)

print(f"Low-stakes game rows: {g['game_low_stakes'].sum():,}")
```

## 3. EDA — Key predictors

### Vegas spread accuracy baseline

Before building any model it is worth establishing what the betting market already
knows. The spread favourite wins ~71% of the time across 2018–2025 regular season
Weeks 1–17. This is the baseline the model must beat.

```{python}
#| label: fig-vegas-baseline
#| fig-cap: "Vegas spread accuracy by season (favourite = team with positive spread_line_team)."

vegas_by_season = (
    played.assign(
        vegas_pred=lambda df: (df["spread_line_team"] > 0).astype(int),
        vegas_correct=lambda df: (
            (df["spread_line_team"] > 0).astype(int) == df["win"].astype(int)
        ).astype(int)
    )
    .groupby("season")["vegas_correct"]
    .mean()
    .reset_index()
    .rename(columns={"vegas_correct": "acc"})
)

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Bar(
    x=vegas_by_season["season"], y=vegas_by_season["acc"],
    marker_color=AMBER, marker_line_width=0,
    text=(vegas_by_season["acc"]*100).round(1).astype(str)+"%",
    textposition="outside"))
fig.add_hline(y=vegas_by_season["acc"].mean(), line_dash="dot",
              line_color=SLATE, line_width=1.2,
              annotation_text=f"Avg {vegas_by_season['acc'].mean():.1%}",
              annotation_position="right", annotation_font_color=SLATE)
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis=dict(title="Season", dtick=1, tickangle=-45),
    yaxis=dict(title="Vegas accuracy (spread)", tickformat=".0%", range=[0.6, 0.8]))
clean_fig(fig).show()
```

# Part II — Modeling

## 4. Offensive & defensive ELO system

Standard team-level ELO treats offenses and defenses as a single unit. This
implementation separates them into **offensive and defensive ELO ratings** that
decouple unit quality. Four pre-game numbers per row —
`team_off_elo`, `team_def_elo`, `opp_off_elo`, `opp_def_elo` — serve as model
features.

**ELO update signal: net yards per play.** The update signal is **net yards per play** (passing
and rushing combined, net of sack yards), which captures both facets of
offensive efficiency in a single number. An offense finishing above the
season-to-date prior-week rolling median YPP earns an ELO "win"; below median
earns the defense an ELO "win." The coupled structure is preserved: each game
updates both the offensive ELO of the team and the defensive ELO of the
opponent.

**Median strategy (leakage-free):** Week 1 uses a historical fallback of
5.5 net YPP (the approximate 2018–2024 grand median). From Week 2 onward, the
threshold is the median of all per-week YPP medians from Weeks 1…W-1 of the
*current* season — purely historical, never incorporating the current game's
data.

```{python}
#| label: elo
#| code-summary: "Compute offensive and defensive ELO ratings"

def compute_elo(g, K=20, INIT=1500, REGRESS=1/3):
    """
    Yards-per-play ELO system.

    Signal
    ------
    Uses net yards per play (yds_per_play) as the update signal:

        yds_per_play = (net_pass_yards + rush_yards) / (dropbacks + carries)

    where net_pass_yards = pass_yards - sack_yards, so sacks penalise the
    offense. This collapses passing AND rushing efficiency into one number
    without requiring arbitrary weighting. An offense that finishes above
    the season-to-date prior-week rolling median YPP is a "win" for the
    offensive ELO; below median is a "win" for the defensive ELO.

    Median strategy — no leakage
    ----------------------------
    Week 1 : hardcoded grand-median fallback (~5.5 net YPP historically).
             No current-season data is available yet.
    Week W : median of the per-week YPP medians from Weeks 1 … W-1 of the
             CURRENT season. This is a season-to-date rolling median that
             never uses any data from Week W or later — clean pre-game info.

    The fallback of 5.5 is derived from the historical 2018-2024 grand
    median net YPP across all team-games. Update this if the dataset window
    changes substantially.

    ELO structure (unchanged)
    -------------------------
    Two ratings per team: off_elo (offensive efficiency) and def_elo
    (defensive efficiency). The expected score for off_elo[t1] vs def_elo[t2]
    follows the standard ELO formula. Season-to-season: ratings regress 1/3
    of the way back to INIT=1500 before Week 1 of a new season.
    """
    off_elo = {t: INIT for t in g["team"].unique()}
    def_elo = {t: INIT for t in g["team"].unique()}

    # ── Build season-to-date prior-week rolling median YPP ───────────────────
    # Step 1: compute the cross-game median YPP for every (season, week) pair.
    #         This uses only games already played in that week — fine, because
    #         the median is only USED to update ELO for future weeks.
    played_g = (g[g["yds_per_play"].notna()]
                .sort_values(["season", "week", "game_id"]))

    wk_med_list = {}
    for (season, week), grp in played_g.groupby(["season", "week"]):
        wk_med_list[(season, week)] = grp["yds_per_play"].median()

    # Step 2: for each (season, week), the comparison threshold is the median
    #         of all per-week medians from Weeks 1 … W-1 in that season.
    #         Week 1 → no prior data → use historical fallback of 5.5.
    YPP_FALLBACK = 5.5   # approximate historical net YPP grand median
    all_season_weeks = sorted(wk_med_list.keys())
    weekly_med = {}
    season_running = {}   # season -> [wk1_med, wk2_med, ...]
    for (season, week) in all_season_weeks:
        prev_weeks = season_running.get(season, [])
        if prev_weeks:
            # median of prior-week medians — purely historical, no leakage
            weekly_med[(season, week)] = float(np.median(prev_weeks))
        else:
            # Week 1: no within-season data yet; use grand-median fallback
            weekly_med[(season, week)] = YPP_FALLBACK
        season_running.setdefault(season, []).append(wk_med_list[(season, week)])

    # ── Process games in strict chronological order ───────────────────────────
    game_order = (g.sort_values(["season", "week", "game_id"])
                   .drop_duplicates("game_id", keep="first")
                   [["game_id", "season", "week"]])

    records = {}
    prev_season = None

    for _, gr in game_order.iterrows():
        gid, season, week = gr["game_id"], gr["season"], gr["week"]

        # Season-boundary regression: pull ratings 1/3 back toward INIT
        if prev_season is not None and season != prev_season:
            for t in list(off_elo):
                off_elo[t] = off_elo[t] * (1 - REGRESS) + INIT * REGRESS
                def_elo[t] = def_elo[t] * (1 - REGRESS) + INIT * REGRESS
        prev_season = season

        rows = g[g["game_id"] == gid]
        teams = rows["team"].tolist()
        if len(teams) != 2:
            continue
        t1, t2 = teams[0], teams[1]
        for t in [t1, t2]:
            off_elo.setdefault(t, INIT)
            def_elo.setdefault(t, INIT)

        # ── Snapshot PRE-GAME ratings (no leakage) ────────────────────────────
        for t, opp in [(t1, t2), (t2, t1)]:
            records[(gid, t)] = {
                "game_id": gid, "team": t,
                "team_off_elo": off_elo[t],   "team_def_elo": def_elo[t],
                "opp_off_elo":  off_elo[opp],  "opp_def_elo":  def_elo[opp]}

        # ── ELO update using yds_per_play ─────────────────────────────────────
        ypp_vals = {row["team"]: row["yds_per_play"]
                    for _, row in rows.iterrows()
                    if pd.notna(row["yds_per_play"])}
        if t1 not in ypp_vals or t2 not in ypp_vals:
            continue
        ypp1 = ypp_vals[t1]
        ypp2 = ypp_vals[t2]
        med  = weekly_med.get((season, week), YPP_FALLBACK)

        # Offense t1 vs Defense t2
        # "win" for off_t1 = t1's YPP > season-to-date median
        # "win" for def_t2 = t1's YPP < season-to-date median (same event)
        exp1   = 1 / (1 + 10**((def_elo[t2] - off_elo[t1]) / 400))
        delta1 = K * ((1.0 if ypp1 > med else 0.0) - exp1)
        off_elo[t1] += delta1
        def_elo[t2] -= delta1   # symmetric: def gets credit when off underperforms

        # Offense t2 vs Defense t1
        exp2   = 1 / (1 + 10**((def_elo[t1] - off_elo[t2]) / 400))
        delta2 = K * ((1.0 if ypp2 > med else 0.0) - exp2)
        off_elo[t2] += delta2
        def_elo[t1] -= delta2

    elo_df = pd.DataFrame(records.values())
    elo_df["off_elo_diff"]   = elo_df["team_off_elo"] - elo_df["opp_def_elo"]
    elo_df["def_elo_diff"]   = elo_df["team_def_elo"] - elo_df["opp_off_elo"]
    elo_df["total_elo_diff"] = elo_df["off_elo_diff"] + elo_df["def_elo_diff"]
    return elo_df

elo_df = compute_elo(g)
print(f"Off ELO range: {elo_df['team_off_elo'].min():.0f} – {elo_df['team_off_elo'].max():.0f}")
print(f"Def ELO range: {elo_df['team_def_elo'].min():.0f} – {elo_df['team_def_elo'].max():.0f}")
# Sanity check: median YPP used as threshold for each season
print("\nSeason-to-date YPP medians used as ELO thresholds (sample):")
played_check = g[g["yds_per_play"].notna()]
for season in sorted(played_check["season"].unique())[-3:]:
    s = played_check[played_check["season"]==season]
    print(f"  {season}: overall median YPP = {s['yds_per_play'].median():.2f} | "
          f"range {s['yds_per_play'].min():.1f}–{s['yds_per_play'].max():.1f}")
```

## 5. Rolling pre-game features

```{python}
#| label: rolling
#| code-summary: "Compute rolling features — dual window, leakage-free SOS, TO split"

def compute_rolling(g):
    REGRESS   = 1/3
    EWMA_SPAN = 4

    off_cols = ["net_ypa","comp_pct","yds_per_carry","third_down_rate",
                "turnovers_total","first_downs_total","time_of_possession_sec",
                "pressure_rate","bad_throw_rate","yac_per_carry",
                "rush_yards","pass_yards","point_diff_capped"]
    def_cols = ["def_comp_pct","def_yds_per_tgt","def_pressure_rate",
                "def_miss_tkl_pct","def_sacks","def_ints","def_yac_allowed"]
    all_cols  = list(dict.fromkeys(off_cols + def_cols))

    # Renamed from 'played' to avoid shadowing the outer played variable
    g_played = g[g["win"].notna()].copy().sort_values(["season","week","team"])

    lg_mean_nypa    = g_played.groupby("season")["net_ypa"].mean().to_dict()
    lg_mean_def_yds = g_played.groupby("season")["def_yds_per_tgt"].mean().to_dict()

    seas_avg_nypa    = g_played.groupby(["season","team"])["net_ypa"].mean()
    seas_avg_def_yds = g_played.groupby(["season","team"])["def_yds_per_tgt"].mean()

    prior_nypa    = {}
    prior_def_yds = {}
    for (season, team), val in seas_avg_nypa.items():
        lm = lg_mean_nypa.get(season, np.nan)
        prior_nypa[(season + 1, team)] = (
            val * (1 - REGRESS) + lm * REGRESS if pd.notna(val) and pd.notna(lm) else lm)
    for (season, team), val in seas_avg_def_yds.items():
        lm = lg_mean_def_yds.get(season, np.nan)
        prior_def_yds[(season + 1, team)] = (
            val * (1 - REGRESS) + lm * REGRESS if pd.notna(val) and pd.notna(lm) else lm)

    opp_nypa_lookup    = {}
    opp_def_yds_lookup = {}

    for (team, season), grp in g_played.groupby(["team","season"]):
        grp = grp.sort_values("week").copy()
        nypa_rolled    = grp["net_ypa"].expanding().mean().shift(1)
        def_yds_rolled = grp["def_yds_per_tgt"].expanding().mean().shift(1)
        seed_nypa    = prior_nypa.get(   (season, team), lg_mean_nypa.get(season, np.nan))
        seed_def_yds = prior_def_yds.get((season, team), lg_mean_def_yds.get(season, np.nan))
        nypa_rolled    = nypa_rolled.fillna(seed_nypa)
        def_yds_rolled = def_yds_rolled.fillna(seed_def_yds)
        for week, nypa_val, def_val in zip(grp["week"], nypa_rolled, def_yds_rolled):
            opp_nypa_lookup[   (season, team, week)] = nypa_val
            opp_def_yds_lookup[(season, team, week)] = def_val

    g_played["opp_roll_nypa"] = g_played.apply(
        lambda r: opp_nypa_lookup.get(
            (r["season"], r["opponent"], r["week"]),
            lg_mean_nypa.get(r["season"], np.nan)), axis=1)
    g_played["opp_roll_def_yds"] = g_played.apply(
        lambda r: opp_def_yds_lookup.get(
            (r["season"], r["opponent"], r["week"]),
            lg_mean_def_yds.get(r["season"], np.nan)), axis=1)

    g_played["nypa_sos"]    = g_played["net_ypa"]         - g_played["opp_roll_nypa"]
    g_played["def_yds_sos"] = g_played["def_yds_per_tgt"] - g_played["opp_roll_def_yds"]

    sos_cols      = ["nypa_sos","def_yds_sos"]
    all_roll_cols = all_cols + sos_cols

    seas_avg_full = g_played.groupby(["season","team"])[all_roll_cols].mean()
    # League mean computed per season using only that season's games — correct for
    # seeding the NEXT season. e.g. lg_mean_full[2024] seeds 2025 Week 1.
    # We do NOT use a cross-season league mean to avoid even minor contamination.
    lg_mean_full  = g_played.groupby("season")[all_roll_cols].mean()

    prior_fill = {}
    for (season, team), row in seas_avg_full.iterrows():
        # lm is the league average FOR season S, used to regress team S avg toward
        # before seeding season S+1. This is always historically known — correct.
        lm = lg_mean_full.loc[season]
        prior_fill[(season + 1, team)] = {
            c: (row[c] * (1 - REGRESS) + lm[c] * REGRESS
                if pd.notna(row[c]) and pd.notna(lm[c]) else lm.get(c, np.nan))
            for c in all_roll_cols}

    g_played = g_played.sort_values(["team","season","week"])
    parts  = []
    ewm_cols = ["net_ypa","def_yds_per_tgt","point_diff_capped",
                "third_down_rate","turnovers_total","pressure_rate"]

    for (team, season), grp in g_played.groupby(["team","season"]):
        grp = grp.sort_values("week").copy()
        for c in all_roll_cols:
            rolled = grp[c].expanding().mean().shift(1)
            fill   = prior_fill.get((season, team), {}).get(c, np.nan)
            grp[f"roll_{c}"] = rolled.fillna(fill)
        for c in ewm_cols:
            ewm_r = grp[c].ewm(span=EWMA_SPAN, adjust=False).mean().shift(1)
            fill  = prior_fill.get((season, team), {}).get(c, np.nan)
            grp[f"roll_ewm_{c}"] = ewm_r.fillna(fill)
        for c in ["def_ints","fumbles_lost"]:
            rolled = grp[c].expanding().mean().shift(1)
            fill   = prior_fill.get((season, team), {}).get(c, np.nan)
            grp[f"roll_{c}_split"] = rolled.fillna(fill)

        out_cols = (["game_id","team"]
                    + [f"roll_{c}" for c in all_roll_cols]
                    + [f"roll_ewm_{c}" for c in ewm_cols]
                    + ["roll_def_ints_split","roll_fumbles_lost_split"])
        parts.append(grp[[c for c in out_cols if c in grp.columns]])

    roll = pd.concat(parts, ignore_index=True)

    # Unplayed-game rolling fill uses the LAST known rolling value
    # per team (not a mean of raw stats), correctly respecting shift(1) ordering.
    unplayed = g[(g["season"] == 2025) & g["win"].isna()]
    if len(unplayed) > 0:
        roll_c = [c for c in roll.columns if c not in ["game_id","team"]]
        # For each team, take the last available rolled row from the played 2025 slice
        played_25_roll = (
            g_played[g_played["season"] == 2025][["game_id","team","week"]]
            .merge(roll, on=["game_id","team"], how="left")
            .sort_values(["team","week"])
        )
        latest_roll = (played_25_roll.groupby("team")[roll_c]
                       .last().reset_index())
        rows = []
        for _, r in unplayed.iterrows():
            team_row = latest_roll[latest_roll["team"] == r["team"]]
            entry = {"game_id": r["game_id"], "team": r["team"]}
            if len(team_row) > 0:
                for c in roll_c:
                    entry[c] = team_row[c].values[0]
            else:
                for c in roll_c:
                    entry[c] = np.nan
            rows.append(entry)
        roll = pd.concat([roll, pd.DataFrame(rows)], ignore_index=True)

    return roll

roll_df = compute_rolling(g)

# ── Build full feature matrix ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
feat = g[["game_id","team","opponent","season","week",
          "is_home","rest","opp_rest","win","point_diff","net_rest_diff",
          "is_division_game","point_diff_capped",
          "spread_line_team","total_line","team_score","opp_score",
          "net_ypa"]].copy()

feat = feat.merge(roll_df, on=["game_id","team"], how="left")

opp_roll = roll_df.rename(columns={"team":"opponent"})
opp_roll.columns = [
    c if c in ["game_id","opponent"] else f"opp_{c}"
    for c in opp_roll.columns]
feat = feat.merge(opp_roll, on=["game_id","opponent"], how="left")
feat = feat.merge(elo_df,   on=["game_id","team"],     how="left")

# Matchup differentials
diff_pairs = [
    ("roll_net_ypa",          "opp_roll_net_ypa"),
    ("roll_comp_pct",         "opp_roll_comp_pct"),
    ("roll_turnovers_total",  "opp_roll_turnovers_total"),
    ("roll_third_down_rate",  "opp_roll_third_down_rate"),
    ("roll_pressure_rate",    "opp_roll_pressure_rate"),
    ("roll_yac_per_carry",    "opp_roll_yac_per_carry"),
]
for tc, oc in diff_pairs:
    feat[f"diff_{tc.replace('roll_','')}"] = feat[tc] - feat[oc]

feat["matchup_pass_eff"] = feat["roll_net_ypa"]       - feat["opp_roll_def_yds_per_tgt"]
feat["matchup_pressure"] = feat["roll_pressure_rate"] - feat["opp_roll_def_pressure_rate"]
feat["diff_nypa_sos"]    = feat["roll_nypa_sos"]    - feat["opp_roll_nypa_sos"]
feat["diff_def_yds_sos"] = feat["roll_def_yds_sos"] - feat["opp_roll_def_yds_sos"]

# Stakes flags
stakes_cols = ["game_id","team","team_clinched","team_eliminated",
               "opp_clinched","opp_eliminated","game_low_stakes"]
feat = feat.merge(g[stakes_cols], on=["game_id","team"], how="left")
for col in ["team_clinched","team_eliminated","opp_clinched",
            "opp_eliminated","game_low_stakes"]:
    feat[col] = feat[col].fillna(0).astype(int)

feat["is_week18"] = (feat["week"] == 18).astype(int)

print(f"Feature matrix: {feat.shape[0]:,} rows x {feat.shape[1]} columns")
```

```{python}
FEATURES = [
    # ELO
    "total_elo_diff", "off_elo_diff", "def_elo_diff",
    "team_off_elo", "team_def_elo",
    # Matchup differentials (expanding rolling)

    "roll_def_ints", "roll_def_sacks",

    "roll_ewm_point_diff_capped", "roll_ewm_third_down_rate",
    "roll_ewm_turnovers_total", "roll_ewm_pressure_rate",
    # Forced vs unforced turnover split
    "roll_def_ints_split",
    "roll_fumbles_lost_split",
    # Context
    "is_home", "rest", "opp_rest", "week",
    "net_rest_diff", "is_division_game",
    # Playoff-stakes flags
    "team_clinched", "team_eliminated",
    "opp_clinched",  "opp_eliminated",
]

# ── Vegas-augmented features — adds spread and total ─────────────────────────
FEATURES_VEGAS = FEATURES + ["spread_line_team", "total_line"]

print(f"Base features:  {len(FEATURES)}")
print(f"Vegas features: {len(FEATURES_VEGAS)}")
```

# Part III — Model Comparison (No Vegas)

## 7. Train / test split

All models use the same split:

- **Train:** 2018–2024, Weeks 1–17 only
- **Test:** 2025, Weeks 1–17 only (in-season; rows without a result yet are skipped)
- **Week 18:** evaluated separately in Section 8b

::: {.callout-important}
**XGBoost early-stopping validation set.**  
To prevent leakage, an internal out-of-time (OOT) validation slice
(2023–2024 Weeks 1–17) is carved from the training window and used exclusively
for early stopping. The 2025 test set is never seen during any part of training.
:::

```{python}
#| label: split
#| code-summary: "Define train/test masks — with OOT validation slice for XGBoost early stopping"

# ── Primary masks ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
train_mask = (feat["season"].between(2018, 2024)
              & feat["win"].notna()
              & (feat["week"] != 18))

test_mask  = ((feat["season"] == 2025)
              & feat["win"].notna()
              & (feat["week"] != 18))

w18_mask   = ((feat["season"] == 2025)
              & feat["win"].notna()
              & (feat["week"] == 18))

# ── Internal OOT validation slice (last 2 seasons of training window) ─────────
# Used ONLY for XGBoost early stopping — never for reporting accuracy.
# Splitting by season (rather than random rows) preserves time ordering and
# prevents temporal leakage inside the training window.
oot_mask   = (feat["season"].isin([2023, 2024])
              & feat["win"].notna()
              & (feat["week"] != 18))
core_mask  = (feat["season"].between(2018, 2022)
              & feat["win"].notna()
              & (feat["week"] != 18))

# Imputation median is always computed on the FULL training window (not just core),
# so it is stable and unaffected by the OOT split.
train_med_feat  = feat.loc[train_mask, FEATURES].median()
train_med_featv = feat.loc[train_mask, FEATURES_VEGAS].median()

X_train = feat.loc[train_mask, FEATURES].fillna(train_med_feat)
y_train_cls = feat.loc[train_mask, "win"]
y_train_reg = feat.loc[train_mask, "point_diff"]

X_test  = feat.loc[test_mask, FEATURES].fillna(train_med_feat)
y_test_cls  = feat.loc[test_mask, "win"]
y_test_reg  = feat.loc[test_mask, "point_diff"]

X_w18   = feat.loc[w18_mask, FEATURES].fillna(train_med_feat)
y_w18   = feat.loc[w18_mask, "win"]

# OOT slice (for early stopping only)
X_oot   = feat.loc[oot_mask, FEATURES].fillna(train_med_feat)
y_oot_cls = feat.loc[oot_mask, "win"]
y_oot_reg = feat.loc[oot_mask, "point_diff"]

# Vegas versions
X_train_v = feat.loc[train_mask, FEATURES_VEGAS].fillna(train_med_featv)
X_test_v  = feat.loc[test_mask,  FEATURES_VEGAS].fillna(train_med_featv)
X_w18_v   = feat.loc[w18_mask,   FEATURES_VEGAS].fillna(train_med_featv)
X_oot_v   = feat.loc[oot_mask,   FEATURES_VEGAS].fillna(train_med_featv)
y_oot_cls_v = feat.loc[oot_mask, "win"]
y_oot_reg_v = feat.loc[oot_mask, "point_diff"]

print(f"Train (full):   {len(X_train):,} rows  |  Test: {len(X_test):,} rows  |  W18: {len(X_w18):,} rows")
print(f"OOT val slice:  {len(X_oot):,} rows  (2023–2024 W1-17, early-stopping only)")

# ── Game-level accuracy helper ────────────────────────────────────────────────
def game_level_accuracy(test_df, pred_col, truth_col="win", id_col="game_id"):
    """
    Deduplicate to one prediction per game before computing accuracy.

    Why this matters
    ----------------
    Each game appears twice in the dataset (once per team). Because
    win_A = 1 - win_B, any model that is self-consistent (predicts A as
    favourite <=> predicts B as underdog) will score identical accuracy on
    team-rows vs game-rows. However a non-linear model like XGBoost is NOT
    constrained to be antisymmetric — it can predict both teams as favourites
    or both as underdogs for the same game. In those cases one row is correct
    and one is wrong. Measuring accuracy on team-rows therefore gives a
    potentially inflated number vs Vegas, which by construction picks exactly
    one winner per game (spread_line_team > 0 for exactly one team).

    Fix: keep only the home-team row for each game (arbitrary but consistent)
    and compute accuracy on that deduplicated set. This is a strict game-level
    metric comparable to the Vegas spread baseline.
    """
    # Keep one row per game — home team perspective (is_home == 1)
    home_rows = test_df[test_df["is_home"] == 1].copy()
    if len(home_rows) == 0:
        # fallback: keep first row per game
        home_rows = test_df.drop_duplicates(id_col, keep="first").copy()
    correct = (home_rows[pred_col] == home_rows[truth_col]).mean()
    return correct, len(home_rows)

print("game_level_accuracy() helper defined")
```

## 7b. Leakage audit

::: {.callout-important}
**Data leakage audit.** Before reporting any accuracy numbers it is worth
being explicit about what could cause inflated results and confirming each is
handled correctly. A model that leaks future information into its training or
test features will produce accuracy numbers that are impossible to replicate
in live deployment, which undermines the entire analysis.

| Risk | How it would leak | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Rolling features** | Using game N stats to predict game N | `.shift(1)` applied to every expanding mean and EWM; Week 1 seeded from prior season ✅ |
| **SOS adjustment** | Normalising game N by opponent's full-season average | Pre-game rolling opponent quality used; Week 1 seeded from prior season ✅ |
| **ELO update** | Recording post-game ELO as pre-game feature | ELO snapshot taken *before* update in every game loop ✅ |
| **Playoff stakes flags** | Using final-season clinch/elimination status | True pre-game snapshot built by processing games in chronological order ✅ |
| **Train/test contamination** | Imputing test NAs with test median | `fillna` uses train-split median only; applied separately to test set ✅ |
| **Target in features** | `point_diff`, `team_score`, `win` accessible in feat table | None appear in `FEATURES` or `FEATURES_VEGAS` lists ✅ |
| **Vegas lines as non-vegas features** | `spread_line_team` leaking into base model | Excluded from `FEATURES`; only in `FEATURES_VEGAS` ✅ |
| **2025 data contaminating train** | Full-dataset median/mean used for seeding | Rolling seeds use only prior-season averages; train median computed on train rows only ✅ |
| **XGBoost early stopping on test set** | `eval_set=[(X_test, y_test)]` tunes rounds to 2025 | OOT slice (2023–2024) used for early stopping; 2025 test never seen during training ✅ |

**Note on the accuracy numbers.** Results at ~77-79% are higher than raw Vegas (~71%). This is plausible because:
(1) the model uses ELO + multiple rolling efficiency metrics that together carry
genuine signal, (2) the 2025 season may be somewhat predictable (few
major upsets in competitive games so far), and (3) the Vegas baseline in this dataset
excludes ties and games with missing spreads which may shift the denominator.
The model should be presented honestly as competitive with but not definitively
beating Vegas — a cross-season test across multiple years would be the right
validation for that claim.
:::

```{python}
#| label: leakage-check
#| code-summary: "Programmatic leakage checks"

# ── 1. Confirm no target columns in feature lists ─────────────────────────────
target_cols  = ["win", "point_diff", "team_score", "opp_score", "point_diff_capped"]
bad_base     = [c for c in target_cols if c in FEATURES]
bad_vegas    = [c for c in target_cols if c in FEATURES_VEGAS]
print("Target cols in FEATURES:       ", bad_base  if bad_base  else "none ✅")
print("Target cols in FEATURES_VEGAS: ", bad_vegas if bad_vegas else "none ✅")

# ── 2. Confirm vegas features not in base model ───────────────────────────────
vegas_only = ["spread_line_team", "total_line"]
leaked_vegas = [c for c in vegas_only if c in FEATURES]
print("Vegas cols in base FEATURES:   ", leaked_vegas if leaked_vegas else "none ✅")

# ── 3. Confirm rolling features are shift(1) by checking Week 1 values ────────
# For Week 1 games the rolling feature should equal the prior-season seed,
# not the current game's stat. Check that roll_net_ypa at Week 1 != net_ypa.
w1 = feat[(feat["week"] == 1) & feat["win"].notna() & feat["roll_net_ypa"].notna()].copy()
same_as_current = (w1["roll_net_ypa"].round(4) == w1["net_ypa"].round(4)).sum()
print(f"\nWeek 1 rows where roll_net_ypa == net_ypa (should be ~0): {same_as_current}")
print(f"  (any non-zero value here would indicate a shift() failure)")

# ── 4. Confirm stakes flags are pre-game (Week 1 teams should all be 0) ───────
w1_stakes = feat[feat["week"] == 1][["team_clinched","team_eliminated",
                                      "opp_clinched","opp_eliminated"]].sum()
print(f"\nWeek 1 stakes flags (all should be 0):")
print(w1_stakes.to_string())

# ── 5. Check train/test date boundaries ───────────────────────────────────────
print(f"\nTrain seasons: {feat.loc[train_mask, 'season'].unique().tolist()}")
print(f"Test seasons:  {feat.loc[test_mask,  'season'].unique().tolist()}")
print(f"Train weeks:   {sorted(feat.loc[train_mask, 'week'].unique().tolist())}")
print(f"Test weeks:    {sorted(feat.loc[test_mask,  'week'].unique().tolist())}")

# ── 6. Confirm imputation uses train median only ──────────────────────────────
train_med = feat.loc[train_mask, FEATURES].median()
test_med  = feat.loc[test_mask,  FEATURES].median()
max_diff  = (train_med - test_med).abs().max()
print(f"\nMax diff between train and test medians: {max_diff:.4f}")
print("  (non-zero confirms test was NOT used to compute imputation values)")
```

## 8. Model suite — win / loss classification

Five model types are compared on direct win/loss prediction.
XGBoost and Random Forest are **non-linear** tree ensembles; Logistic Regression
with L2 penalty is a **linear** classifier. This contrast is useful when
presenting: the gap between linear and non-linear accuracy shows how much the
relationships in the data depart from linearity.

::: {.callout-important}
**Walk-forward cross-validation for hyperparameter selection.**  
Hyperparameters are selected via a time-series-aware CV grid search. Each fold
trains on seasons up to year S and validates on year S+1, covering seasons
2019→2020, 2020→2021, 2021→2022, and 2022→2023. The best hyperparameters are
then used to train the final model on the **full 2018–2024 window**. This
preserves temporal order, avoids leakage, and gives a principled basis for the
chosen configuration. XGBoost early stopping inside each CV fold also uses the
fold's validation split — never the 2025 test set.
:::

```{python}
#| label: train-classifiers
#| code-summary: "Walk-forward CV hyperparameter search + final classifier training"

from xgboost import XGBClassifier
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression, RidgeClassifier
from sklearn.metrics import (accuracy_score, brier_score_loss,
                             log_loss, roc_auc_score)
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from itertools import product as iterproduct

# ── Walk-forward CV folds: train on [2018..S], validate on [S+1] ─────────────
WF_FOLDS = [
    (list(range(2018, 2020)), 2020),
    (list(range(2018, 2021)), 2021),
    (list(range(2018, 2022)), 2022),
    (list(range(2018, 2023)), 2023),
]

def wf_mask(feat, train_seasons, val_season, week_excl=18):
    tr = (feat["season"].isin(train_seasons) & feat["win"].notna()
          & (feat["week"] != week_excl))
    vl = ((feat["season"] == val_season)     & feat["win"].notna()
          & (feat["week"] != week_excl))
    return tr, vl

def wf_cv_score(feat, features, model_fn, param_dict):
    """
    Walk-forward CV accuracy for a given model factory and hyperparams.
    model_fn(params) → fitted model.  Imputation uses fold train median only.

    Scaler handling
    ---------------
    Some model factories (MLP, Logistic Regression) fit a StandardScaler on
    Xtr and store it as mdl._scaler_cv. The validation set Xvl must be
    transformed by the SAME fitted scaler — not refit on Xvl — before
    calling predict_proba. Failing to do this causes the MLP to predict on
    unscaled data despite being trained on scaled data, which depresses CV
    accuracy and may lead to incorrect hyperparameter selection.
    This fix checks for _scaler_cv and applies it to Xvl when present.
    """
    fold_accs = []
    for tr_seasons, val_season in WF_FOLDS:
        tr_m, vl_m = wf_mask(feat, tr_seasons, val_season)
        med = feat.loc[tr_m, features].median()
        Xtr = feat.loc[tr_m, features].fillna(med).values
        ytr = feat.loc[tr_m, "win"].values
        Xvl = feat.loc[vl_m, features].fillna(med).values
        yvl = feat.loc[vl_m, "win"].values
        mdl = model_fn(param_dict, Xtr, ytr)
        # Apply factory scaler to val set if the model stored one
        if hasattr(mdl, "_scaler_cv"):
            Xvl_pred = mdl._scaler_cv.transform(Xvl)
        else:
            Xvl_pred = Xvl
        if hasattr(mdl, "predict_proba"):
            preds = (mdl.predict_proba(Xvl_pred)[:, 1] >= 0.5).astype(int)
        else:
            preds = mdl.predict(Xvl_pred)
            preds = (preds > 0).astype(int) if preds.dtype == float else preds
        fold_accs.append(accuracy_score(yvl, preds))
    return float(np.mean(fold_accs))

# ── XGBoost CV grid ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
xgb_grid = list(iterproduct(
    [3, 4],          # max_depth
    [0.03, 0.05],    # learning_rate
    [0.6, 0.8],      # subsample
))

def _xgb_cls_factory(p, Xtr, ytr):
    """Train XGBoost classifier; OOT split inside fold used for early stopping."""
    n = len(Xtr)
    split = int(n * 0.85)   # last 15% of fold-train as mini early-stop val
    Xe, ye = Xtr[split:], ytr[split:]
    Xtr2, ytr2 = Xtr[:split], ytr[:split]
    m = XGBClassifier(
        n_estimators=600, max_depth=p[0], learning_rate=p[1],
        subsample=p[2], colsample_bytree=0.6, min_child_weight=15,
        reg_alpha=1.0, reg_lambda=5.0, gamma=1.0,
        random_state=42, eval_metric="logloss", early_stopping_rounds=40,
        verbosity=0)
    m.fit(Xtr2, ytr2, eval_set=[(Xe, ye)], verbose=False)
    return m

print("XGBoost CV search …")
best_xgb_params, best_xgb_score = None, -1
for p in xgb_grid:
    sc = wf_cv_score(feat, FEATURES, _xgb_cls_factory, p)
    if sc > best_xgb_score:
        best_xgb_score, best_xgb_params = sc, p
print(f"  best params: max_depth={best_xgb_params[0]}, lr={best_xgb_params[1]}, "
      f"subsample={best_xgb_params[2]}  →  CV acc={best_xgb_score:.4f}")

# ── Random Forest CV grid ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
rf_grid = list(iterproduct([5, 6, 8], [15, 25]))  # max_depth, min_samples_leaf

def _rf_cls_factory(p, Xtr, ytr):
    m = RandomForestClassifier(
        n_estimators=500, max_depth=p[0], min_samples_leaf=p[1],
        max_features="sqrt", random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
    m.fit(Xtr, ytr)
    return m

print("Random Forest CV search …")
best_rf_params, best_rf_score = None, -1
for p in rf_grid:
    sc = wf_cv_score(feat, FEATURES, _rf_cls_factory, p)
    if sc > best_rf_score:
        best_rf_score, best_rf_params = sc, p
print(f"  best params: max_depth={best_rf_params[0]}, min_samples_leaf={best_rf_params[1]}"
      f"  →  CV acc={best_rf_score:.4f}")

# ── Logistic Regression CV grid ───────────────────────────────────────────────
lr_C_grid = [0.1, 0.5, 1.0, 5.0]

def _lr_cls_factory(p, Xtr, ytr):
    sc = StandardScaler(); Xtr_sc = sc.fit_transform(Xtr)
    m = LogisticRegression(C=p[0], max_iter=1000, random_state=42)
    m.fit(Xtr_sc, ytr)
    m._scaler_cv = sc
    return m

print("Logistic Regression CV search …")
best_lr_C, best_lr_score = None, -1
for p in [(c,) for c in lr_C_grid]:
    sc = wf_cv_score(feat, FEATURES, _lr_cls_factory, p)
    if sc > best_lr_score:
        best_lr_score, best_lr_C = sc, p[0]
print(f"  best C={best_lr_C}  →  CV acc={best_lr_score:.4f}")

# ── Ridge Classifier CV grid ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
ridge_alpha_grid = [0.1, 1.0, 10.0, 50.0]

def _ridge_cls_factory(p, Xtr, ytr):
    sc = StandardScaler(); Xtr_sc = sc.fit_transform(Xtr)
    m = RidgeClassifier(alpha=p[0])
    m.fit(Xtr_sc, ytr)
    return m

print("Ridge Classifier CV search …")
best_ridge_alpha, best_ridge_score = None, -1
for p in [(a,) for a in ridge_alpha_grid]:
    sc = wf_cv_score(feat, FEATURES, _ridge_cls_factory, p)
    if sc > best_ridge_score:
        best_ridge_score, best_ridge_alpha = sc, p[0]
print(f"  best alpha={best_ridge_alpha}  →  CV acc={best_ridge_score:.4f}")

# ── MLP (Neural Network) CV grid ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# MLPClassifier is sklearn's feedforward network.
# Architecture search: hidden layer sizes and regularisation alpha.
# Scaling is applied inside the factory since MLP requires normalised inputs.
from sklearn.neural_network import MLPClassifier

mlp_grid = list(iterproduct(
    [(64, 32), (128, 64), (64, 32, 16)],   # hidden_layer_sizes
    [0.0001, 0.001, 0.01],                  # alpha (L2 regularisation)
))

def _mlp_cls_factory(p, Xtr, ytr):
    sc = StandardScaler()
    Xtr_sc = sc.fit_transform(Xtr)
    m = MLPClassifier(
        hidden_layer_sizes=p[0], alpha=p[1],
        activation="relu", solver="adam",
        max_iter=500, random_state=42,
        early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.12,
        n_iter_no_change=20, tol=1e-4,
        shuffle=False)   # temporal val split: last 12% of fold-train rows
    m.fit(Xtr_sc, ytr)
    m._scaler_cv = sc
    return m

print("MLP (Neural Network) CV search …")
best_mlp_params, best_mlp_score = None, -1
for p in mlp_grid:
    sc = wf_cv_score(feat, FEATURES, _mlp_cls_factory, p)
    if sc > best_mlp_score:
        best_mlp_score, best_mlp_params = sc, p
print(f"  best hidden_layers={best_mlp_params[0]}, alpha={best_mlp_params[1]}"
      f"  →  CV acc={best_mlp_score:.4f}")

# ── Final model training on full 2018-2024 window ────────────────────────────
# XGBoost: OOT slice (X_oot) used for early stopping — 2025 test never touched
scaler_cls = StandardScaler()
X_train_sc = scaler_cls.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_sc  = scaler_cls.transform(X_test)

xgb_cls = XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=600, max_depth=best_xgb_params[0],
    learning_rate=best_xgb_params[1], subsample=best_xgb_params[2],
    colsample_bytree=0.6, min_child_weight=15,
    reg_alpha=1.0, reg_lambda=5.0, gamma=1.0,
    random_state=42, eval_metric="logloss", early_stopping_rounds=40,
    verbosity=0)
xgb_cls.fit(X_train, y_train_cls,
            eval_set=[(X_oot, y_oot_cls)], verbose=False)

rf_cls = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=500, max_depth=best_rf_params[0],
    min_samples_leaf=best_rf_params[1],
    max_features="sqrt", random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
rf_cls.fit(X_train, y_train_cls)

lr_cls = LogisticRegression(C=best_lr_C, max_iter=1000, random_state=42)
lr_cls.fit(X_train_sc, y_train_cls)

ridge_cls = RidgeClassifier(alpha=best_ridge_alpha)
ridge_cls.fit(X_train_sc, y_train_cls)

# MLP: scaler fitted on full training window — separate from scaler_cls
# so each model owns its own normalisation and they don't interfere
scaler_mlp = StandardScaler()
X_train_mlp = scaler_mlp.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_mlp  = scaler_mlp.transform(X_test)

# shuffle=False so the early-stopping val split takes the LAST 12% of the
# training window (temporally most recent rows ≈ late 2024) rather than a
# random stratified sample. This is more appropriate for time-series data.
mlp_cls = MLPClassifier(
    hidden_layer_sizes=best_mlp_params[0], alpha=best_mlp_params[1],
    activation="relu", solver="adam",
    max_iter=500, random_state=42,
    early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.12,
    n_iter_no_change=20, tol=1e-4,
    shuffle=False)
mlp_cls.fit(X_train_mlp, y_train_cls)
print(f"MLP trained: {len(mlp_cls.loss_curve_)} iterations | "
      f"best val loss={min(mlp_cls.validation_scores_):.4f}")

# ── Vegas baseline ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
vegas_pred = (feat.loc[test_mask, "spread_line_team"] > 0).astype(int)

# ── Collect metrics ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def cls_metrics(model, X_tr, X_te, y_tr, y_te, scaled=False, is_ridge=False,
                test_df_ref=None):
    """
    Collect classifier metrics. Reports both team-row accuracy (for reference)
    and game-level accuracy (primary metric, one prediction per game).
    test_df_ref: the feat slice for the test mask, used for game-level dedup.
    """
    if is_ridge:
        prob_te = None
        pred_te = model.predict(X_te)
        pred_tr = model.predict(X_tr)
    else:
        prob_te = model.predict_proba(X_te)[:, 1]
        prob_tr = model.predict_proba(X_tr)[:, 1]
        pred_te = (prob_te >= 0.5).astype(int)
        pred_tr = (prob_tr >= 0.5).astype(int)
    acc_te_row = accuracy_score(y_te, pred_te)    # team-row accuracy
    acc_tr     = accuracy_score(y_tr, pred_tr)
    auc        = roc_auc_score(y_te, prob_te) if prob_te is not None else np.nan
    brier      = brier_score_loss(y_te, prob_te) if prob_te is not None else np.nan
    ll         = log_loss(y_te, prob_te) if prob_te is not None else np.nan

    # Game-level accuracy (primary)
    if test_df_ref is not None:
        tmp = test_df_ref.copy()
        tmp["_pred"] = pred_te
        acc_te_game, _ = game_level_accuracy(tmp, "_pred", "win")
    else:
        acc_te_game = acc_te_row   # fallback if ref not provided

    return {
        "Test Acc (game)":  round(acc_te_game, 4),   # PRIMARY
        "Test Acc (row)":   round(acc_te_row,  4),   # reference
        "Train Accuracy":   round(acc_tr, 4),
        "Train-Test Gap":   round(acc_tr - acc_te_game, 4),
        "AUC-ROC":    round(auc,   4) if not np.isnan(auc)   else "—",
        "Brier Score": round(brier, 4) if not np.isnan(brier) else "—",
        "Log Loss":    round(ll,   4) if not np.isnan(ll)    else "—",
        "_prob": prob_te,
        "_pred": pred_te,
    }

# ── Game-level Vegas baseline (primary — one unique prediction per game) ──────
test_df_ref   = feat.loc[test_mask].copy()
home_test     = test_df_ref[test_df_ref["is_home"] == 1]
vegas_acc_game = accuracy_score(
    home_test["win"],
    (home_test["spread_line_team"] > 0).astype(int))
vegas_acc_row  = accuracy_score(       # team-row reference
    test_df_ref["win"],
    (test_df_ref["spread_line_team"] > 0).astype(int))
# keep vegas_acc as alias for downstream code
vegas_acc = vegas_acc_game

results_cls = {
    "XGBoost":             cls_metrics(xgb_cls,   X_train,     X_test,
                                       y_train_cls, y_test_cls, test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "Random Forest":       cls_metrics(rf_cls,    X_train,     X_test,
                                       y_train_cls, y_test_cls, test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "Logistic Regression": cls_metrics(lr_cls,    X_train_sc,  X_test_sc,
                                       y_train_cls, y_test_cls, scaled=True,
                                       test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "Ridge Classifier":    cls_metrics(ridge_cls, X_train_sc,  X_test_sc,
                                       y_train_cls, y_test_cls,
                                       scaled=True, is_ridge=True,
                                       test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "Neural Network (MLP)": cls_metrics(mlp_cls,  X_train_mlp, X_test_mlp,
                                        y_train_cls, y_test_cls,
                                        test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
}

display_cols = ["Test Acc (game)", "Test Acc (row)", "Train Accuracy",
                "Train-Test Gap", "AUC-ROC", "Brier Score", "Log Loss"]
tbl = pd.DataFrame({k: {c: v[c] for c in display_cols}
                     for k, v in results_cls.items()}).T
tbl.index.name = "Model"
tbl["vs Vegas"] = (tbl["Test Acc (game)"].astype(float) - vegas_acc_game).round(4)
print(f"Vegas — game-level: {vegas_acc_game:.4f} | team-row: {vegas_acc_row:.4f}")
print("(Primary metric is game-level — one independent prediction per game)\n")
print(tbl.to_string())
```


```{python}
#| label: fig-mlp-training
#| code-summary: "MLP training loss curve diagnostic"
#| fig-cap: "MLP training and validation loss curves. Convergence pattern and early-stopping point indicate whether the network is over/under-fitting."

fig = go.Figure()
fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
    x=list(range(1, len(mlp_cls.loss_curve_) + 1)),
    y=mlp_cls.loss_curve_,
    mode="lines", name="Training loss",
    line=dict(color=BLUE, width=2)))
if hasattr(mlp_cls, "validation_scores_") and mlp_cls.validation_scores_:
    # validation_scores_ is accuracy; convert to rough proxy loss for visual
    val_loss = [1 - s for s in mlp_cls.validation_scores_]
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=list(range(1, len(val_loss) + 1)),
        y=val_loss,
        mode="lines", name="Validation loss (1 − acc)",
        line=dict(color=AMBER, width=2, dash="dash")))
fig.add_vline(x=mlp_cls.best_loss_ if (hasattr(mlp_cls, "best_loss_") and mlp_cls.best_loss_ is not None) else len(mlp_cls.loss_curve_),
              line_dash="dot", line_color=SLATE, line_width=1.2,
              annotation_text="Early stop", annotation_font_color=SLATE)
fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Epoch", yaxis_title="Loss",
    showlegend=True,
    legend=dict(x=0.65, y=0.95, bgcolor="rgba(255,255,255,0.85)"))
clean_fig(fig, height=380).show()
```

::: {.callout-note}
**Linear vs non-linear: the presentation story.** Tree ensembles (XGBoost,
Random Forest) can capture interaction effects — e.g. that a strong pass rush
matters more against a team with a bad offensive line. Linear models (Logistic
Regression, Ridge) assume each feature adds independently. The accuracy gap
between these two families quantifies how much interaction structure exists in
NFL game outcomes. If the gap is small, the underlying relationships are
approximately linear and a simpler model would suffice. If it is large, the
non-linear structure is real and the added complexity of a tree model is
justified.
:::

## 9. Model suite — point differential regression

Rather than predicting win/loss directly, these models predict the **actual
point margin** (e.g. +7 or −3). A predicted margin > 0 is mapped back to a
predicted win. This two-step approach sometimes outperforms direct classification
because the regression target carries more information — a model that predicts
+14 vs +1 has learned something that a binary label collapses.

```{python}
#| label: train-regressors
#| code-summary: "Walk-forward CV hyperparameter search + final regressor training"

from xgboost import XGBRegressor
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression, Ridge
from sklearn.metrics import mean_absolute_error, mean_squared_error
from sklearn.neural_network import MLPRegressor

def wf_cv_score_reg(feat, features, model_fn, param_dict):
    """Walk-forward CV MAE for regressors."""
    fold_maes = []
    for tr_seasons, val_season in WF_FOLDS:
        tr_m, vl_m = wf_mask(feat, tr_seasons, val_season)
        med = feat.loc[tr_m, features].median()
        Xtr = feat.loc[tr_m, features].fillna(med).values
        ytr = feat.loc[tr_m, "point_diff"].values
        Xvl = feat.loc[vl_m, features].fillna(med).values
        yvl = feat.loc[vl_m, "point_diff"].values
        mdl = model_fn(param_dict, Xtr, ytr)
        preds = mdl.predict(Xvl)
        fold_maes.append(mean_absolute_error(yvl, preds))
    return float(np.mean(fold_maes))

# ── XGBoost Regressor CV grid ────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _xgb_reg_factory(p, Xtr, ytr):
    n = len(Xtr); split = int(n * 0.85)
    m = XGBRegressor(
        n_estimators=600, max_depth=p[0], learning_rate=p[1],
        subsample=p[2], colsample_bytree=0.6, min_child_weight=15,
        reg_alpha=1.0, reg_lambda=5.0, gamma=1.0,
        random_state=42, eval_metric="rmse", early_stopping_rounds=40,
        verbosity=0)
    m.fit(Xtr[:split], ytr[:split],
          eval_set=[(Xtr[split:], ytr[split:])], verbose=False)
    return m

print("XGBoost Regressor CV search …")
best_xgb_reg_params, best_xgb_reg_mae = None, np.inf
for p in xgb_grid:
    mae = wf_cv_score_reg(feat, FEATURES, _xgb_reg_factory, p)
    if mae < best_xgb_reg_mae:
        best_xgb_reg_mae, best_xgb_reg_params = mae, p
print(f"  best params: depth={best_xgb_reg_params[0]}, lr={best_xgb_reg_params[1]}, "
      f"sub={best_xgb_reg_params[2]}  →  CV MAE={best_xgb_reg_mae:.3f} pts")

# ── RF Regressor CV grid ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _rf_reg_factory(p, Xtr, ytr):
    m = RandomForestRegressor(
        n_estimators=500, max_depth=p[0], min_samples_leaf=p[1],
        max_features="sqrt", random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
    m.fit(Xtr, ytr); return m

print("Random Forest Regressor CV search …")
best_rf_reg_params, best_rf_reg_mae = None, np.inf
for p in rf_grid:
    mae = wf_cv_score_reg(feat, FEATURES, _rf_reg_factory, p)
    if mae < best_rf_reg_mae:
        best_rf_reg_mae, best_rf_reg_params = mae, p
print(f"  best params: depth={best_rf_reg_params[0]}, min_leaf={best_rf_reg_params[1]}"
      f"  →  CV MAE={best_rf_reg_mae:.3f} pts")

# ── Ridge Regression CV grid ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
def _ridge_reg_factory(p, Xtr, ytr):
    sc = StandardScaler(); Xtr_sc = sc.fit_transform(Xtr)
    m = Ridge(alpha=p[0]); m.fit(Xtr_sc, ytr); return m

print("Ridge Regression CV search …")
best_ridge_reg_alpha, best_ridge_reg_mae = None, np.inf
for a in ridge_alpha_grid:
    mae = wf_cv_score_reg(feat, FEATURES, _ridge_reg_factory, (a,))
    if mae < best_ridge_reg_mae:
        best_ridge_reg_mae, best_ridge_reg_alpha = mae, a
print(f"  best alpha={best_ridge_reg_alpha}  →  CV MAE={best_ridge_reg_mae:.3f} pts")

# ── Final regressor training on full 2018-2024 window ────────────────────────
scaler_reg = StandardScaler()
X_train_sc_r = scaler_reg.fit_transform(X_train)
X_test_sc_r  = scaler_reg.transform(X_test)

xgb_reg = XGBRegressor(
    n_estimators=600, max_depth=best_xgb_reg_params[0],
    learning_rate=best_xgb_reg_params[1], subsample=best_xgb_reg_params[2],
    colsample_bytree=0.6, min_child_weight=15,
    reg_alpha=1.0, reg_lambda=5.0, gamma=1.0,
    random_state=42, eval_metric="rmse", early_stopping_rounds=40, verbosity=0)
xgb_reg.fit(X_train, y_train_reg,
            eval_set=[(X_oot, y_oot_reg)], verbose=False)

rf_reg = RandomForestRegressor(
    n_estimators=500, max_depth=best_rf_reg_params[0],
    min_samples_leaf=best_rf_reg_params[1],
    max_features="sqrt", random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
rf_reg.fit(X_train, y_train_reg)

ols_reg = LinearRegression()
ols_reg.fit(X_train_sc_r, y_train_reg)

ridge_reg = Ridge(alpha=best_ridge_reg_alpha)
ridge_reg.fit(X_train_sc_r, y_train_reg)

# ── MLP Regressor (reuse CV-tuned architecture from classifier search) ────────
mlp_reg = MLPRegressor(
    hidden_layer_sizes=best_mlp_params[0], alpha=best_mlp_params[1],
    activation="relu", solver="adam",
    max_iter=500, random_state=42,
    early_stopping=True, validation_fraction=0.12,
    n_iter_no_change=20, tol=1e-4)
mlp_reg.fit(X_train_mlp, y_train_reg)
print(f"MLP Regressor trained: {len(mlp_reg.loss_curve_)} iterations")

# ── Collect metrics ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def reg_metrics(model, X_tr, X_te, y_tr_cls, y_te_cls, y_tr_reg, y_te_reg,
                test_df_ref=None):
    pred_margin_te = model.predict(X_te)
    pred_margin_tr = model.predict(X_tr)
    pred_win_te    = (pred_margin_te > 0).astype(int)
    pred_win_tr    = (pred_margin_tr > 0).astype(int)
    acc_row = accuracy_score(y_te_cls, pred_win_te)
    acc_tr  = accuracy_score(y_tr_cls, pred_win_tr)

    # Game-level accuracy
    if test_df_ref is not None:
        tmp = test_df_ref.copy()
        tmp["_pred"] = pred_win_te
        acc_game, _ = game_level_accuracy(tmp, "_pred", "win")
    else:
        acc_game = acc_row

    return {
        "Test Acc (game)":            round(acc_game, 4),
        "Test Acc (row)":             round(acc_row, 4),
        "Train Accuracy (converted)": round(acc_tr, 4),
        "Train-Test Gap":             round(acc_tr - acc_game, 4),
        "Test MAE (pts)":             round(mean_absolute_error(y_te_reg, pred_margin_te), 3),
        "Test RMSE (pts)":            round(np.sqrt(mean_squared_error(y_te_reg, pred_margin_te)), 3),
        "_pred": pred_win_te,
        "_margin": pred_margin_te,
    }

results_reg = {
    "XGBoost Regressor":  reg_metrics(xgb_reg,   X_train,      X_test,
                                      y_train_cls, y_test_cls, y_train_reg, y_test_reg,
                                      test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "Random Forest Reg":  reg_metrics(rf_reg,    X_train,      X_test,
                                      y_train_cls, y_test_cls, y_train_reg, y_test_reg,
                                      test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "OLS":                reg_metrics(ols_reg,   X_train_sc_r, X_test_sc_r,
                                      y_train_cls, y_test_cls, y_train_reg, y_test_reg,
                                      test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "Ridge Regression":   reg_metrics(ridge_reg, X_train_sc_r, X_test_sc_r,
                                      y_train_cls, y_test_cls, y_train_reg, y_test_reg,
                                      test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "Neural Network (MLP)": reg_metrics(mlp_reg, X_train_mlp,  X_test_mlp,
                                        y_train_cls, y_test_cls, y_train_reg, y_test_reg,
                                        test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
}

reg_display_cols = ["Test Acc (game)", "Test Acc (row)", "Train Accuracy (converted)",
                    "Train-Test Gap", "Test MAE (pts)", "Test RMSE (pts)"]
tbl_reg = pd.DataFrame({k: {c: v[c] for c in reg_display_cols}
                          for k, v in results_reg.items()}).T
tbl_reg.index.name = "Model"
tbl_reg["vs Vegas"] = (tbl_reg["Test Acc (game)"].astype(float) - vegas_acc_game).round(4)
print(f"Vegas — game-level: {vegas_acc_game:.4f}\n")
print(tbl_reg.to_string())
```

## 10. Select best non-vegas model

The model with the highest test accuracy across **both** classification and
point-differential tables is selected as the non-vegas champion for downstream
projections and cap analysis.

```{python}
#| label: select-best-noveg
#| code-summary: "Select best non-vegas model"

# Map model names to their fitted objects and scalers for downstream use
cls_model_map = {
    "XGBoost":              (xgb_cls,   None),
    "Random Forest":        (rf_cls,    None),
    "Logistic Regression":  (lr_cls,    scaler_cls),
    "Ridge Classifier":     (ridge_cls, scaler_cls),
    "Neural Network (MLP)": (mlp_cls,   scaler_mlp),
}
reg_model_map = {
    "XGBoost Regressor":    (xgb_reg,   None),
    "Random Forest Reg":    (rf_reg,    None),
    "OLS":                  (ols_reg,   scaler_reg),
    "Ridge Regression":     (ridge_reg, scaler_reg),
    "Neural Network (MLP)": (mlp_reg,   scaler_mlp),
}

all_noveg = {}
for name, res in results_cls.items():
    mdl, scl = cls_model_map[name]
    all_noveg[f"[CLS] {name}"] = {
        "acc": res["Test Acc (game)"],
        "pred": res["_pred"],
        "prob": res.get("_prob"),
        "type": "classifier",
        "_model": mdl,
        "_scaler": scl,
        "_features": FEATURES,
        "_has_proba": True,
    }
for name, res in results_reg.items():
    mdl, scl = reg_model_map[name]
    all_noveg[f"[REG] {name}"] = {
        "acc": res["Test Acc (game)"],
        "pred": res["_pred"],
        "prob": None,
        "type": "regressor",
        "_model": mdl,
        "_scaler": scl,
        "_features": FEATURES,
        "_has_proba": False,
    }

best_noveg_name = max(all_noveg, key=lambda k: all_noveg[k]["acc"])
best_noveg      = all_noveg[best_noveg_name]

print(f"Best non-vegas model: {best_noveg_name}")
print(f"Test accuracy:        {best_noveg['acc']:.4f}")
print(f"vs Vegas:             {best_noveg['acc'] - vegas_acc:+.4f}")
```

---

# Part IV — Vegas-Augmented Model Suite

::: {.callout-warning}
**Why include a vegas model?** The original model is built without market data
because the *purpose* of the project is to see how well publicly available team
performance metrics can predict outcomes — using vegas lines is, in a sense,
"cheating" since the spread already aggregates information from sharp bettors.
That said, adding the spread as a feature is a legitimate benchmarking exercise:
it shows the accuracy ceiling when market information is available, and the SHAP
collinearity analysis below reveals which of our performance features become
redundant once the market's information is included.
:::

## 11. Vegas model suite — win / loss classification

```{python}
#| label: train-classifiers-vegas
#| code-summary: "Train all classifiers with vegas features — CV-tuned params, OOT early stopping"

# Vegas CV search — same grid, same WF folds, but over FEATURES_VEGAS
def wf_cv_score_v(feat, model_fn, param_dict):
    return wf_cv_score(feat, FEATURES_VEGAS, model_fn, param_dict)

print("XGBoost (vegas) CV search …")
best_xgb_v_params, best_xgb_v_score = None, -1
for p in xgb_grid:
    sc = wf_cv_score_v(feat, _xgb_cls_factory, p)
    if sc > best_xgb_v_score:
        best_xgb_v_score, best_xgb_v_params = sc, p
print(f"  best: depth={best_xgb_v_params[0]}, lr={best_xgb_v_params[1]}  →  CV={best_xgb_v_score:.4f}")

print("RF (vegas) CV search …")
best_rf_v_params, best_rf_v_score = None, -1
for p in rf_grid:
    sc = wf_cv_score_v(feat, _rf_cls_factory, p)
    if sc > best_rf_v_score:
        best_rf_v_score, best_rf_v_params = sc, p
print(f"  best: depth={best_rf_v_params[0]}, min_leaf={best_rf_v_params[1]}  →  CV={best_rf_v_score:.4f}")

print("Logistic (vegas) CV search …")
best_lr_v_C, best_lr_v_score = None, -1
for c in lr_C_grid:
    sc = wf_cv_score_v(feat, _lr_cls_factory, (c,))
    if sc > best_lr_v_score:
        best_lr_v_score, best_lr_v_C = sc, c
print(f"  best C={best_lr_v_C}  →  CV={best_lr_v_score:.4f}")

print("Ridge (vegas) CV search …")
best_ridge_v_alpha, best_ridge_v_score = None, -1
for a in ridge_alpha_grid:
    sc = wf_cv_score_v(feat, _ridge_cls_factory, (a,))
    if sc > best_ridge_v_score:
        best_ridge_v_score, best_ridge_v_alpha = sc, a
print(f"  best alpha={best_ridge_v_alpha}  →  CV={best_ridge_v_score:.4f}")

print("MLP (vegas) CV search …")
best_mlp_v_params, best_mlp_v_score = None, -1
for p in mlp_grid:
    sc = wf_cv_score_v(feat, _mlp_cls_factory, p)
    if sc > best_mlp_v_score:
        best_mlp_v_score, best_mlp_v_params = sc, p
print(f"  best hidden_layers={best_mlp_v_params[0]}, alpha={best_mlp_v_params[1]}"
      f"  →  CV acc={best_mlp_v_score:.4f}")

# Final training
scaler_cls_v = StandardScaler()
X_train_sc_v = scaler_cls_v.fit_transform(X_train_v)
X_test_sc_v  = scaler_cls_v.transform(X_test_v)

xgb_cls_v = XGBClassifier(
    n_estimators=600, max_depth=best_xgb_v_params[0],
    learning_rate=best_xgb_v_params[1], subsample=best_xgb_v_params[2],
    colsample_bytree=0.6, min_child_weight=15,
    reg_alpha=1.0, reg_lambda=5.0, gamma=1.0,
    random_state=42, eval_metric="logloss", early_stopping_rounds=40, verbosity=0)
xgb_cls_v.fit(X_train_v, y_train_cls,
              eval_set=[(X_oot_v, y_oot_cls_v)], verbose=False)

rf_cls_v = RandomForestClassifier(
    n_estimators=500, max_depth=best_rf_v_params[0],
    min_samples_leaf=best_rf_v_params[1],
    max_features="sqrt", random_state=42, n_jobs=-1)
rf_cls_v.fit(X_train_v, y_train_cls)

lr_cls_v = LogisticRegression(C=best_lr_v_C, max_iter=1000, random_state=42)
lr_cls_v.fit(X_train_sc_v, y_train_cls)

ridge_cls_v = RidgeClassifier(alpha=best_ridge_v_alpha)

                                              y_train_cls, y_test_cls, test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "Logistic Regression (vegas)": cls_metrics(lr_cls_v,    X_train_sc_v, X_test_sc_v,
                                              y_train_cls, y_test_cls, scaled=True,
                                              test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
    "Ridge Classifier (vegas)":    cls_metrics(ridge_cls_v, X_train_sc_v, X_test_sc_v,
                                              y_train_cls, y_test_cls,
                                              scaled=True, is_ridge=True,

    "Neural Network (MLP) (vegas)": cls_metrics(mlp_cls_v, X_train_mlp_v, X_test_mlp_v,
                                                y_train_cls, y_test_cls,
                                                test_df_ref=test_df_ref),
}

tbl_v = pd.DataFrame({k: {c: v[c] for c in display_cols}
                       for k, v in results_cls_v.items()}).T
```

## 14. SHAP collinearity analysis — vegas features

When spread and total line are added to the feature set, some performance
metrics become redundant — the market has already priced them in. The SHAP
bar chart below shows which features retain independent importance after
vegas lines are included, and which drop toward zero.

VIF (Variance Inflation Factor) quantifies linear multicollinearity between
features. A VIF > 10 indicates strong collinearity; values between 5–10 are
moderate. Features with high VIF after adding vegas lines are the ones the
market most efficiently encodes.

```{python}
#| label: shap-vegas
#| code-summary: "SHAP + VIF for best vegas classifier"

import shap
from statsmodels.stats.outliers_influence import variance_inflation_factor

# ── SHAP (on XGBoost vegas model for interpretability) ───────────────────────
xgb_for_shap = xgb_cls_v  # XGBoost always used for SHAP regardless of best model

explainer_v   = shap.TreeExplainer(xgb_for_shap)
rng           = np.random.RandomState(42)
idx_v         = rng.choice(len(X_train_v), min(800, len(X_train_v)), replace=False)
shap_vals_v   = explainer_v.shap_values(X_train_v.iloc[idx_v])
feat_vals_v   = X_train_v.iloc[idx_v].values

mean_shap_v = (pd.Series(np.abs(shap_vals_v).mean(0), index=FEATURES_VEGAS)
               .sort_values(ascending=False))

# ── VIF ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
X_vif = X_train_v.copy().fillna(X_train_v.median())
vif_data = pd.DataFrame({
    "Feature": FEATURES_VEGAS,
    "VIF": [variance_inflation_factor(X_vif.values, i)
            for i in range(X_vif.shape[1])]
}).sort_values("VIF", ascending=False)

print("Top 15 features by VIF (vegas model):")
print(vif_data.head(15).to_string(index=False))
```

```{python}
def norm_to_rgb(v):
    r = int(220 * v + 37 * (1 - v))
    g_c = int(38  * v + 99 * (1 - v))
    b = int(38  * v + 235* (1 - v))

    fv  = feat_vals_v[:, fi]
    fv_min, fv_max = np.nanpercentile(fv, 5), np.nanpercentile(fv, 95)
    fv_norm  = np.where(np.isnan(fv), 0.5,
                   np.clip((fv - fv_min) / (fv_max - fv_min + 1e-9), 0, 1))
    dot_colors = [norm_to_rgb(v) for v in fv_norm]
    y_jitter   = yi + rng2.uniform(-0.35, 0.35, size=len(sv))

    border_color = RED if feat_name in ["spread_line_team","total_line"] else None

    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
```
